speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific patterns to your rash, such as it appearing in waves or spreading from one area to another?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the sparing of the perioral area is a significant clue. Given the recent viral prodrome and the facial rash, have you noticed any joint pain, muscle aches, or changes in urine color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.
